facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The Income Tax Department on Friday clarified that individuals holding foreign bank accounts with an aggregate balance of up to Rs 20 lakh at any point during the previous year will not be required to file a declaration under the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), provided the funds in those accounts come from disclosed sources.
facts.text: Individuals holding foreign bank accounts with an aggregate balance of up to Rs 20 lakh funded by disclosed sources are exempt from filing declarations under FAST-DS.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, taxpayers holding one or more foreign bank accounts with an aggregate balance of up to Rs 20 lakh at any point during the previous year are exempt from the Rs 10 lakh penalty for non-disclosure in Schedule FA of the ITR.
facts.text: Taxpayers with qualifying foreign bank accounts of up to Rs 20 lakh are protected from a penalty of Rs 10 lakh under the Black Money Act for non-disclosure in Schedule FA.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Under the scheme, taxpayers are required to pay 30% tax on the value of the undisclosed foreign asset or income, along with an additional amount equivalent to the tax, taking the effective levy to 60%.
facts.text: Taxpayers regularising undisclosed foreign assets or income must pay a baseline tax of 30 percent.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Under the scheme, taxpayers are required to pay 30% tax on the value of the undisclosed foreign asset or income, along with an additional amount equivalent to the tax, taking the effective levy to 60%.
facts.text: The combined levy on undisclosed overseas assets under Category A amounts to an effective rate of 60 percent.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Category A covers undisclosed assets located outside India or foreign income that was not offered to tax, subject to an aggregate asset value of up to Rs 1 crore.
facts.text: Category A declarations for undisclosed offshore assets or untaxed overseas earnings are capped at an aggregate value of Rs 1 crore.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The monetary threshold for declarations under this category is Rs 5 crore, with a flat fee of Rs 1 lakh.
facts.text: Category B allows individuals to regularise previously taxed foreign assets not reported in Schedule FA up to an aggregate ceiling of Rs 5 crore.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The monetary threshold for declarations under this category is Rs 5 crore, with a flat fee of Rs 1 lakh.
facts.text: Eligible individuals declaring accounted overseas assets under Category B must pay a flat regularisation fee of Rs 1 lakh.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: In its supplementary FAQs, the department also clarified that an exchange rate of Rs 94.6543 per US dollar, applicable as of March 30, 2026, will be used to calculate the fair market value of foreign assets.
facts.text: The Income Tax Department set the reference conversion rate at Rs 94.6543 per US dollar for determining the fair market value of foreign assets.

topic.summary: The Income Tax Department has announced exemptions for individuals with foreign bank accounts under FAST-DS. Individuals with balances up to Rs 20 lakh from disclosed sources do not need to file declarations. This exemption applies as long as the accounts contain no undisclosed income or unaccounted deposits. The scheme provides a one-time opportunity to disclose foreign assets and income by December 31.
